title: Unique algebraization of a coherent map with adic torsion error
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ a Noetherian algebraic space over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-sfb-space-coherent-adic-system], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use quasi-coherent modules on the small etale ringed site [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]; coherent means coherent on etale scheme charts [pqf-def-coherent]. Let $L\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ be a quasi-coherent ideal, let $H$ be coherent and let $P\in\mathrm{Coh}(X,L)$ [def-sfb-space-coherent-adic-system]. Suppose $u:P\to\widehat H_L$ is a morphism and there is $t\geq1$ such that $L^t$ kills the ordinary sheaf kernel and cokernel of every $u_n$. Then there exist a coherent module $E$, a module map $b:E\to H$ whose ordinary kernel and cokernel are killed by some positive power of $L$, and an isomorphism $\gamma:P\xrightarrow{\sim}\widehat E_L$ such that $u=\widehat b_L\gamma$. The triple $(E,b,\gamma)$ is unique up to unique isomorphism: for any two such triples there is exactly one module isomorphism $v:E\xrightarrow{\sim}E^{\prime}$ with $b^{\prime}v=b$ and $\widehat v_L\gamma=\gamma^{\prime}$.

source.place: Tag 08BB (lemma-existence-easy), existence and uniqueness of the torsion-controlled triple.

proof.text: Choose an etale scheme atlas $V\to X$ and cover $V$ by affine opens. Each affine is Noetherian, by the locally Noetherian chart condition. Their images in $|X|$ are open: the atlas-test lemma makes their inverse images in $V$ open, and the final-topology definition then applies. They cover $|X|$, so quasi-compactness gives finitely many, with scheme coproduct $U$. Its components are open and closed by the scheme-coproduct theorem; the induced map is etale since it is etale on these open components. Thus $p:U\to X$ is a surjective etale atlas with $U$ a Noetherian scheme. A finite disjoint union of Noetherian affine schemes is Noetherian since its components are open and closed. The empty space is handled by the empty atlas. This uses no separation or field hypothesis.

source.place: Tag 03BX (lemma-topology-points), openness of affine-chart images and finite subcover

proof.text: Etale pullback here is restriction on localized sites. Hence it preserves the ordinary sheaf kernels and cokernels and the ideal-action maps. In particular $p^*u$ has its component kernels and cokernels killed by $(p^*L)^t$. The scheme Zariski/etale equivalence is exact, preserves finite presentation and commutes naturally with tensor pullback. Products $L^nM$ are images of the multiplication maps $L^{\otimes n}\otimes M\to M$; exactness and the tensor comparison therefore identify these products and their quotients on both sites. Consequently the equivalence identifies completion diagrams, their transition maps, and the component annihilation hypothesis, not merely the individual underlying modules. On the Noetherian scheme $U$, coherence is the finite-presentation condition tested on affine charts. Apply the scheme torsion-triple theorem to the resulting Zariski data. Return to the etale site to obtain $(E_U,b_U,\gamma_U)$ and $s\ge1$ killing the actual kernel and cokernel of $b_U$. This theorem also gives uniqueness among triples having that actual torsion condition.

source.place: Tag 08BB (lemma-existence-easy), reduction to scheme Tag 0889(1); descent.tex Tags 03DX, 03LC, 06VE, 05VG

proof.text: Put $R=U\times_XU$, with projections $r_1,r_2$. It is a scheme, etale over $U$, by the representable diagonal and etale scheme-test lemma. It is locally Noetherian by the chart convention; we do not assume $R$ affine or globally Noetherian. On each affine open $W\subset R$, the restrictions of $r_1^*(E_U,b_U,\gamma_U)$ and $r_2^*(E_U,b_U,\gamma_U)$ are two torsion-controlled triples for the same restricted $u$. The site comparisons from step 2 preserve these data. The scheme theorem gives the unique isomorphism $a_W:r_1^*E_U|_W\to r_2^*E_U|_W$ preserving $b$ and $\gamma$. On an intersection of two such opens, pass to any affine open inside the intersection; scheme uniqueness makes the two maps equal there. Glue the Zariski maps, and their inverses, by the gluing-morphisms theorem; the site equivalence gives $a$ on $R$. The resulting map is an isomorphism since its composites with the glued inverse are identities on the affine cover. All the required equations hold there and therefore globally.

source.place: Tag 08BB (lemma-existence-easy), uniqueness and etale descent; scheme uniqueness Tag 0889(1), map gluing Tag 04TN

proof.text: On the triple fibre product the two arrows $a_{23}a_{12}$ and $a_{13}$ preserve $b$ and $\gamma$: for the formal comparisons their composites are respectively $\gamma_3\gamma_2^{-1}\gamma_2\gamma_1^{-1}$ and $\gamma_3\gamma_1^{-1}$. On every affine open, scheme uniqueness identifies the arrows. The gluing-morphisms theorem identifies them globally. On the diagonal the same uniqueness identifies $a$ with the identity. Thus $(E_U,a)$ is a groupoid-module descent datum. The quasi-coherent groupoid equivalence descends it to a coherent $E$ on $X$, since $E_U$ is coherent, and descends $b_U$ to $b:E\to H$. For each $n$, the chart calculus identifies the pullback of $E/L^nE$ with $E_U/(p^*L)^nE_U$. The component $\gamma_{U,n}$ commutes with the descent data because $a$ preserves $\gamma_U$; full faithfulness descends it and its inverse to $\gamma_n:P_n\simeq E/L^nE$. Transition compatibility is an equality of module maps checked on $U$ by faithfulness. The same argument descends $u_n=\widehat b_n\gamma_n$. Hence the $\gamma_n$ form the required system isomorphism $\gamma$.

source.place: Tag 08BB (lemma-existence-easy), effective descent; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M3; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 07UB

proof.text: The kernel and cokernel of $b$ are quasi-coherent and their restrictions to $U$ are the actual kernel and cokernel of $b_U$, by the affine-chart calculus. Their multiplication maps by $L^s$ restrict to zero, since step 2 supplied the single exponent $s$ on the whole Noetherian scheme $U$. The faithful groupoid restriction functor therefore makes these multiplication maps zero on $X$. This proves the required global bound on the ordinary sheaf kernel and cokernel of $b$; no assertion that completion is faithful has been used.

source.place: Tag 08BB (lemma-existence-easy), descent of the bounded torsion condition

proof.text: Given any two triples on $X$, their restrictions to $U$ satisfy the scheme theorem, including the actual torsion condition on each algebraic map. It gives a unique $v_U:E_U\simeq E'_U$ with $b'_Uv_U=b_U$ and $\widehat v_U\gamma_U=\gamma'_U$. On $R$, the two descent comparisons of $v_U$ are isomorphisms between the same triples. On every affine open of $R$ they agree by scheme uniqueness; gluing-morphisms uniqueness makes them equal on $R$. Thus $v_U$ respects the groupoid data and descends to an isomorphism $v$. Its two equations can be checked after restriction to $U$, componentwise for the completion equation, and hold by full faithfulness. Any other such $v$ restricts to $v_U$ by scheme uniqueness and equals $v$ by faithfulness. This proves the stated uniqueness for any two triples.

(4) Cocycle on the triple product and identity on the diagonal; groupoid descent (03M3/07UB) gives a coherent E, then b and γ_n by full faithfulness. (5) L^s kills ker and coker b by faithfulness. lean.statement: theorem exists_unique_torsionControlled_algebraization {S : Scheme.{u}} (X : AlgebraicSpace S) (hln : ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, IsLocallyNoetherian (X.etaleForget.obj T)) (hqc : CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj)) (hqs : IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X) (L : QuasiCoherentIdeal X) (H : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (C := X.Modules) (fun M ↦ M.IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, RingedSpace.IsCoherent (X.etaleForget.obj T).toRingedSpace ((X.schemeRestriction T).obj M))) (P : CoherentAdicSystem X L hln hqc hqs) (u : P ⟶ (coherentAdicCompletion L hln hqc hqs).obj H) (htorsion : CoherentAdicKernelCokernelKilled L u.hom) : ∃ (E : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (C := X.Modules) (fun M ↦ M.IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, RingedSpace.IsCoherent (X.etaleForget.obj T).toRingedSpace ((X.schemeRestriction T).obj M))) (b : E ⟶ H) (γ : P ≅ (coherentAdicCompletion L hln hqc hqs).obj E), u = γ.hom ≫ (coherentAdicCompletion L hln hqc hqs).map b ∧ (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧ (∀ k : KernelFork b.hom, IsLimit k → AdicPowerKills L s k.pt) ∧ (∀ c : CokernelCofork b.hom, IsColimit c → AdicPowerKills L s c.pt)) ∧ ∀ (E' : ObjectProperty.FullSubcategory (C := X.Modules) (fun M ↦ M.IsQuasicoherent ∧ ∀ T : X.EtaleSite, RingedSpace.IsCoherent (X.etaleForget.obj T).toRingedSpace ((X.schemeRestriction T).obj M))) (b' : E' ⟶ H) (γ' : P ≅ (coherentAdicCompletion L hln hqc hqs).obj E'), u = γ'.hom ≫ (coherentAdicCompletion L hln hqc hqs).map b' → (∃ s : ℕ, 1 ≤ s ∧ (∀ k : KernelFork b'.hom, IsLimit k → AdicPowerKills L s k.pt) ∧ (∀ c : CokernelCofork b'.hom, IsColimit c → AdicPowerKills L s c.pt)) → ∃! v : E ≅ E', v.hom ≫ b' = b ∧ γ.hom ≫ (coherentAdicCompletion L hln hqc hqs).map v.hom = γ'.hom
